name: Vostok 3KA
notes: Carried Yuri Gagarin, the first human in space (12 Apr 1961). Crew ejected and landed separately under parachute.

name: Mercury
notes: First US crewed spacecraft: two suborbital and four orbital flights. Mass is for orbital flights (Friendship 7).

name: Voskhod
notes: Modified Vostok. Voskhod 2 carried Alexei Leonov on the first spacewalk (18 Mar 1965).

name: Gemini
notes: Two-person spacecraft that proved rendezvous, docking, long-duration flight and EVA ahead of Apollo.

name: Apollo Command and Service Module
notes: Mass is Apollo 11 CSM-107 (command module ≈5,560 kg). Flew to lunar orbit, Skylab and Apollo–Soyuz.

name: Apollo Lunar Module
notes: Only crewed vehicle to land on another world (six landings, 1969–72). Mass is Apollo 11 fully fuelled; later J-mission LMs reached ~16,400 kg.

name: Soyuz 7K-OK
notes: First Soyuz. Soyuz 1 (1967) killed Vladimir Komarov when its parachute failed.

name: Soyuz MS
notes: Latest in a Soyuz lineage flying since 1967; ISS crew transport.

name: Space Shuttle Orbiter
notes: Reusable winged orbiter; five orbital vehicles (Columbia, Challenger, Discovery, Atlantis, Endeavour) plus test article Enterprise. Dry mass varies by orbiter (~78–80 t).

name: Buran (OK-1K1)
notes: Soviet shuttle. One uncrewed fully automatic orbital flight (15 Nov 1988); destroyed in 2002 hangar collapse.

name: Shenzhou
notes: Soyuz-derived but larger; three modules. First crewed flight Shenzhou 5 (Yang Liwei, 2003).

name: Crew Dragon
notes: First privately built crew vehicle to reach orbit (Demo-2, May 2020). Mass is capsule plus trunk; typically flies 4 crew.

name: CST-100 Starliner
notes: Crew Flight Test (2024) returned without crew after thruster problems; further flights under review.

name: Orion MPCV
notes: Artemis crew vehicle with European Service Module. Flew uncrewed on EFT-1 (2014) and Artemis I (2022).

name: Gaganyaan
notes: India's crew capsule, planned for LEO on a human-rated LVM3. Uncrewed test flights preceding crewed mission.

name: Mengzhou
notes: Next-generation Chinese crew spacecraft for LEO and lunar missions; abort tests flown, first orbital flight planned on Long March 10 family.

name: Lanyue
notes: Chinese crewed lunar lander for planned landing before 2030; landing/takeoff tests performed in 2025.

name: Starship HLS
notes: Artemis Human Landing System variant of Starship; requires on-orbit propellant transfer.

name: Blue Moon Mk 2
notes: Crewed lunar lander for Artemis V; Mk 1 is the uncrewed cargo version.

name: Dream Chaser
notes: Uncrewed cargo lifting-body for ISS resupply, launched on Vulcan; a crewed version was proposed.
